title: Content Verification Overrides Vector Score — False Positive Prevention

high_vector_low_content.description: Vector score > 0.6 but content score ≤ 4 (false positive candidates)
high_vector_low_content.fppr_description: 72% of high-vector false positives caught and filtered by content verification

examples.content_reason: Different domain (aerospace vs energy storage), keyword match only

examples.query: behavioral economics cognitive bias decision making

low_vector_high_content.description: Vector score < 0.5 but content score ≥ 6 (rescued candidates)
low_vector_high_content.description_detail: Content verification rescues relevant docs missed by vector similarity

key_findings: 18% of top-20 candidates are high-vector false positives that would degrade precision
Content verification catches 72% of these false positives
8% of candidates are low-vector but content-relevant; 69% of these are rescued
Content verification is the primary mechanism for FPR reduction (from 27.5% to 2.5%)
Fast-exit (score ≥ 6) triggers on 17.5% of evaluations, reducing latency by ~40%
